stem: A coordinator and four research subagents all need the same 300-document source corpus. Pasting it into each subagent's prompt exhausts the context budget. Which MCP capability addresses this?

options.label: A
options.body: MCP resources — the server exposes the documents and each subagent reads only what it needs.
options.rationale: Correct. Resources are server-exposed data an agent pulls on demand, so the corpus is addressed by reference instead of copied into five prompts.

options.label: B
options.body: MCP server-to-server transfer, where the corpus server hands the documents straight to the agents' own server so only one of them pays the loading cost.
options.rationale: MCP servers do not talk to each other. Every exchange goes through the client, which is the host application.

options.label: C
options.body: MCP prompts, configured so the corpus is injected automatically at the start of each subagent's turn.
options.rationale: Prompts are reusable templates the user invokes; injecting 300 documents through them recreates the same context problem.

options.label: D
options.body: None — MCP has no mechanism for shared data, so the corpus must be chunked and threaded through prompts regardless.
options.rationale: Resources exist precisely for this. Chunking through prompts is the workaround the protocol removes the need for.

stem: A document-analysis subagent must determine which of 400 downloaded report files mention "Section 45X". Which built-in tool is the right one?

options.label: A
options.body: Grep — it searches inside file contents for a pattern.
options.rationale: Correct. Grep matches on content across many files at once, which is exactly the question being asked here.

options.label: B
options.body: Glob — it matches file paths against a naming pattern.
options.rationale: Glob finds files by name or path. It cannot see what is written inside them.

options.label: C
options.body: Read — open each of the 400 files in turn and scan them for the phrase.
options.rationale: This reaches the right answer but burns the context window on 400 full documents to learn one fact about each.

options.label: D
options.body: Write — build an index file of the corpus first, then consult that index instead.
options.rationale: Write produces files, it does not search them, and building an index still requires reading the corpus first.

stem: The system exposes one `research` tool that takes a topic and internally searches, fetches, and summarises. When a run fails the coordinator cannot tell which stage broke, nor retry only the fetch. What is the design fix?

options.label: A
options.body: Split it into separate `search`, `fetch`, and `summarise` tools with distinct boundaries.
options.rationale: Correct. A tool is the unit of both failure and retry. Three tools give three places to fail visibly and three things to retry independently.

options.label: B
options.body: Keep the single tool and expand its description so the model has a full account of each of the three stages it runs through internally.
options.rationale: A description explains behaviour but cannot subdivide a call. One invocation still succeeds or fails as one unit.

options.label: C
options.body: Keep the single tool and have it return a longer, more detailed internal log on every invocation.
options.rationale: Better logs aid diagnosis after the fact but still leave the coordinator unable to retry one stage.

options.label: D
options.body: Add a `research_debug` tool that replays the last run so failures can be inspected afterwards.
options.rationale: This adds surface area to inspect a problem the interface should not create, and replay is not recovery.

stem: Every claim in the final report must carry a citation, but the synthesis agent sometimes writes a paragraph in prose and never calls `cite_source`. Which configuration makes the call certain?

options.label: A
options.body: Set `tool_choice` to the specific named tool `cite_source` on the synthesis step.
options.rationale: Correct. Naming a specific tool in tool_choice compels that call. It is the only option here that turns a requirement into a guarantee rather than an instruction.

options.label: B
options.body: Leave `tool_choice` on `auto` and add a strongly worded instruction that every single claim has to be cited without exception.
options.rationale: Under auto the model may still answer in prose. Emphasis in a prompt lowers the failure rate; it does not remove the option.

options.label: C
options.body: Set `tool_choice` to `any`, letting the model pick whichever tool best suits the paragraph.
options.rationale: `any` compels some tool call but not this one, so the agent can satisfy it with an unrelated tool.

options.label: D
options.body: Strip every tool except `cite_source` from the synthesis agent and let `auto` select the only one remaining.
options.rationale: Under `auto` the model can still call nothing at all, and removing the other tools cripples the step's real work.
